newsitem.title: USA: New York museum given 11 major Chinese paintings.
newsitem.headline: New York museum given 11 major Chinese paintings.

text.p: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has received 11 major Chinese paintings, making its Chinese art collection the most comprehensive one outside China and Taiwan, the museum said on Monday.

Museum director Philippe de Montebello said the gift came from Oscar Tang, an investment banker and a member of the institution's board of trustees, who put up the money to buy them. The price was not disclosed.
The paintings, from the C.C. Wang Family Collection, include "The Riverbank," a 10th-century silk scroll that predates all the famous hanging scrolls remaining in China.

"Its acquisition, along with 10 other paintings, marks a momentous event in the history of the Metropolitan," de Montebello said. "Over the past 25 years, thanks to the support of many of our benefactors, the museum has assembled a collection of Chinese painting that reflects the full range of the classical Chinese artistic tradition."

Six of the works will go on display on Thursday, when the museum's permanent galleries of Chinese art reopen after renovation. The museum said the remaining five would be shown later, at a date not yet decided.
The Chinese galleries were expanded and renovated over two years into a 13,400-square-foot (1,245-square-metre) space comprising 14 rooms. The museum said the renovation cost $14 million.

All 11 paintings in the gift come from the collection of the family of 90-year-old painter and collector C.C. Wang, who escaped from China in the early 1950s after the communist revolution. He once considered bartering "The Riverbank" for his son, Shou Kun Wang, who eventually made his way to the United States in 1979 after the Chinese Cultural Revolution.

"The Riverbank" bears the signature of Dong Yuan, a court scholar during the Southern Tang Dynasty who died in 962. The museum called it a landmark work of ink and light colour on silk and the earliest surviving accepted example of monumental Chinese landscape painting.

De Montebello said the work was recognised as one of the rarest monumental landscape paintings in the world and the largest and earliest of three famous scrolls by three great masters. The other two are Fan Kuan's "Travelers Amid Streams and Mountains" and Guo Xi's "Early Spring." Both are in the National Palace Museum in Taiwan.

Wang did not want "The Riverbank" to return to China because of the unpredictable political situation there, and he believed the Metropolitan would provide greater access to the works for visitors than museums in Beijing or Taiwan.

The Chinese galleries will display the Metropolitan's huge collections of Chinese painting, calligraphy, jade, lacquer, textiles, metalwork and other objects dating from the eighth century to the 20th.
